Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our onboarding checklist we need a completed subset of your security questionnaire focused on PII handling and an updated dataflow diagram scoped to the Medisys tenant. We have three asks to unblock our internal approval: 

1) A mapping of PII fields we should expect in logs/telemetry (examples) and which of those are masked, tokenized, hashed, or stored in full by Redwood.
2) A clear delineation of roles with access (Redwood internal vs Medisys-only admin) and whether any Redwood subprocessors have direct access to customer PII.
3) An updated dataflow diagram showing network boundaries, encryption-in-transit/e2e, and where KV caches or ephemeral proxies touch unredacted tokens.

We attempted to enter answers in your SSQ spreadsheet but had a few items where we need clarifications before we finalize. Attaching the Medisys intake sheet and a rough drawing we started. Could you please review and confirm which fields are considered PII by Redwood and where we should expect exportable artifacts for audit?

Alicia — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Priya (Privacy lead), Jonas (Infra security) and Marissa (Customer Engineering) so we can get authoritative answers back to you.

Quick notes before we fill the spreadsheet:
- We treat PII at three tiers for telemetry/export: Sensitive identifiers (SSNs, full credit card numbers), Direct identifiers (email, phone), and Derivative tokens (hashed/email-aliased). We can provide a columnized mapping for each field in your SSQ.
- Regarding subprocessors: Redwood has a limited set of infra subprocessors (cloud providers and a managed metrics vendor). None of our subprocessors have direct access to unredacted customer PII in hosted mode unless explicitly provisioned in a Dedicated/private deployment — we will confirm specifics for the services that touch KV caches.
- For the dataflow diagram, we need the final version of your tenant diagram (thank you for the rough drawio). We'll update it to show: ingress/egress boundaries, prefix/KV cache points, where we perform prefix caching vs full-session storage, and TLS/e2e notes.

Could you confirm two items so we scope answers correctly: 1) Are you evaluating Redwood in Hosted (shared) mode or Dedicated capacity for the first-phase? 2) Do you need token-level audit logs exported to your Splunk/SEIM or will Redwoods' audit artifacts suffice for the initial compliance package?

I'll pick this up with the team and send a consolidated SSQ and an annotated diagram by EOD Wednesday.

Best,

Alicia / team — thanks for the additional context. Below are consolidated answers and attached artifacts. I'll paste the highlights here and attach the annotated diagram and SSQ export (CSV) for your audit pack.

Highlights:
- PII classification: We map fields into three categories (Sensitive, Direct, Derived). In Hosted mode:
  * Sensitive (SSNs, PAN, full bank details) — Redwood does not persist full values in searchable logs; these are redacted at the edge and only stored in encrypted, access-controlled backups if customer elects long-term retention.
  * Direct (email, phone, user_id) — visible to customer tenancy; Redwood retains a hashed token for routing/kv-cache; access is limited to on-call SREs via just-in-time access with audit logging.
  * Derived (hashed identifiers, similarity vectors) — used for caching/indexing only.

- Subprocessors: Our infra subprocessors (cloud provider instances and managed monitoring vendor) do not have direct access to unredacted PII in Hosted mode. For Dedicated/private we provide an HSM/KMS separation and can exclude a monitoring subprocess that accesses tokenized metadata — details in the attached Subprocessor table.

- Access roles and justification:
  * Medisys-admins (customer) — full tenant-level access via RBAC.
  * Redwood SRE/Security — emergency access limited to specific incidents; access requires approval and is scoped to ephemeral sessions.
  * On-call Engineers (customer support) — read-only telemetry, no raw PII.

- Dataflow diagram notes: see annotated image for the points where prefix KV caching occurs (edge cache A), where partial tokenization happens (ingest B), and where audit exports are taken (audit stream -> Splunk). Encryption: TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest; customer KMS supported for Dedicated.

Next steps / deliverables we attached and shared to your drive: 
- redwood-ssq-mapping.csv (completed answers keyed to your SSQ columns)
- annotated_MEDISYS_dataflow.drawio.png (diagram with callouts)
- Subprocessor_evidence.pdf (redacted) — note we will provide SOC2 attestations via secure link once contract is signed.

If you need a short call to walk through the diagram with our infra engineer (Jonas) and privacy lead (Priya), happy to schedule 30 minutes tomorrow. Otherwise we'll upload the formal audit pack into the HubSpot ticket (HS-938426).

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
